glosses: szanować
A rough calculation or assessment of the value, size, or cost of something.

examples.text: “They know our boats will stand up to their work,” said Willison, “and that counts for a good deal. A low estimate from us doesn't mean scamped work, but just that we want to keep the yard busy over a slack time.”

glosses: A rough calculation or assessment of the value, size, or cost of something.
A document (or verbal notification) specifying how much a job is likely to cost.
An upper limitation on some positive quantity.

examples.text: The desired norm estimate is now obtained from the identity... [referring to an earlier statement saying that a certain norm is less than or equal to a certain expression]

glosses: To calculate roughly, often from imperfect data.

examples.text: I estimate that I need 400 board feet of lumber to complete a job, and then order 350 because I do not want a surplus, or perhaps order 450 because I do not want to make any subsequent orders.
Higher real prices for durables are estimated to have reduced their consumption per capita by 1.09% in 1930, […]

glosses: To judge and form an opinion of the value of, from imperfect data.

examples.text: It is by the weight of silver, and not the name of the piece, that men estimate commodities and exchange them.
It is always very difficult to estimate the age in which you are living.

glosses: estimated
To determine, estimate or judge the value of; to evaluate; to estimate.

examples.text: He assessed the situation.
An insurance adjuster will assess the damage.

glosses: To impose or charge, especially as punishment for an infraction.

examples.text: The referee assessed a penalty for delaying the game.
A $10.00 late fee will be assessed on all overdue accounts.

Judge Cohen ruled that Blacklock, McKenzie and Benschop must make restitution for the $50.29 damage and that each must pay a mandatory $40.00 surcharge assessed to anybody who is found guilty of a misdemeanor in New York state.

glosses: To calculate and demand (the tax money due) from a person or entity.

examples.text: Once you've submitted a tax return, the Tax Department will assess the amount of tax you still owe.

glosses: Zahlenwerte, Größen oder Ähnliches aufgrund bekannter Tatsachen näherungsweise bestimmen

examples.text: Er schätzte ihr Alter auf 21 Jahre.
Die Expertin schätzte den Wert auf 500 €.
„Ihr Vermögen […] wird auf 2,2 Milliarden Dollar geschätzt.“
„Für Europa schätzt man um 1600 rund 100 Millionen Einwohner, für Amerika vor den Reisen des Columbus etwa 10 Millionen Einwohner.“

glosses: davon ausgehen, dass etwas so sein wird; vermuten

examples.text: Ich schätze, der wird's nicht mehr lange machen.
Schätze, wir kommen heute zu spät!

glosses: etwas einen hohen Wert zuweisen und es damit gerne mögen

examples.text: Ich schätze es, das Frühstück ans Bett gebracht zu bekommen.
Alten Wein muss man erst schätzen lernen.

glosses: etwas mit einem exakten oder geschätzten Zahlenwert bezeichnen

examples.text: Je nach Messmethode wird der Gehaltsunterschied mal auf 22 Prozent beziffert wie aktuell von der EU, mal auf knapp 30 Prozent wie vom Statistischen Bundesamt, mal irgendwo dazwischen wie von der OECD.

glosses: sich auf einen Wert belaufen, einen Wert erreichen

examples.text: Vorläufig beziffern sich Lunkewitz’ Forderungen angeblich auf 48,8 Millionen Euro Schadensersatz.
